name: 1827 S. Prairie Avenue — the Doane house's coach house (draft refined by T-1936 from the Glessner House print)

function.note: The 1911 sheet reads '2-storey brick BARN on the alley'. 1911 labels it a garage or barn; for 1904 the envelope is backcast and its use reconstructed as a stable/coach house.

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2330, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1936 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 28 trace (s28fp-1827-b2), the T-1841 census (s28-1827-rear) and the T-1837 register row frontage-28-053; every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-18-20-east-2330). T-1936 refines its yard front from the one picture that shows it: the Glessner House blog print of the Doane house (a18-gh-doane-exterior, the same negative as Chicagology's copy, data/sources/chicagology_1827_doane_exterior.json), whose right edge shows the north end of this building's west face past the house's south flank. Read through that print's solved camera (data/reference_views/doane_house_1827_prairie_coach_house/glessner_blog_print.json): pale walls, a flat top under a plain cornice, a belt course at the loft floor, a loft sash under an eared stone hood and a carriage opening under a flat segmental head, with a glazed light in its leaves. Everything the print does not show stays the draft's (liberty L-t1936-doane-coach-house).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s28fp-1827-b2 p1 (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 84% of its fill; s28fp-1827-b2 p1 (main, brick), rectangle 2 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 84% of its fill; s28fp-1827-b2 p1 (main, brick), rectangle 3 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 84% of its fill. Roles: the main part's largest rectangle is the main body; a shallow rectangle at the front is a bay; the sheet's ranges, porches and stone fronts keep their roles. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed). T-1936: r2's cornice is the Glessner House print's thin moulding (about 0.25 m deep, little projection: y 400-404 px at x 540), not the rules' 0.4 m slab; inferred.

draft_elevation.note: T-1936, from the Glessner House print of the Doane house (a18-gh-doane-exterior; source chicagology_1827_doane_exterior), whose right edge (x about 505-561 px) shows the north end of this building's west (yard) face, read through the print's solved camera carried into this frame (reference view glessner_blog_print): at about 16.8 px a metre there, every height measured from the face's foot in the print (y about 490 px). READ FROM THE PRINT (the tier stays reconstructed: this one attribute still carries the draft rules' choices for every face the print does not show, and a pale tone in a toned print is a reading, not a record): the storeys, 3.0 m to the belt and 2.3 m above it (the cornice's top 5.3 m over the foot, the belt course's top 3.1 m, read at x 540 px); the walls' tone, a pale cream (tint), much paler than the house's stone in the same print, taken as the cream brick Chicago builders used (the 1911 sheet says brick; the colour itself is the print's tone, not a record); the dressed face r2:u1: one loft sash 0.75 m wide, sill 3.2 m on the belt, head 4.38 m, under an eared stone hood 1.55 m across to 4.8 m (x 525-550 px, y 409-436); a carriage opening 2.3 m wide (x 522-557 px), springing 2.25 m, its segmental head rising about 0.15 m (y 450-452), its leaves near-black in the print (dark paint, or leaves standing open on a dark room: the door tint), with a pale panel about 0.6 by 1.1 m in them (x 531-541, y 456-475), drawn pale as the print shows it because whether it is a curtained light or a painted panel is not legible at that size; a belt course of about 0.3 m at the loft floor (y 438-443), run on along r1's yard face, which the print does not show. STILL THE DRAFT RULES': the plan (the 1911 sheet's trace), r1's gable roof, every other face, the count of bays the print cannot see (the face's south part, v -5.75 to -4.2 m, is behind the house's flank and is built blank), chimneys none. Liberty L-t1936-doane-coach-house; the draft's L-draft-prairie-18-20-east-2330 no longer covers this face.
